pamphlet_excerpts: Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics: Extending courtesy to other outdoor visitors is a natural habit of backpackers (p. 61).
Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics Principle 2: If you carry amobile telephone for emergency communication, turn it off andstow it in your pack until you need (p. 61).
Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics Principle 3: Appreciate the company of those you meet on the trail and at campsites near yours, butrespect their desire for quiet and solitude (p. 61).
Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics Principle 4: If you encounter horsebackriders or pack animals, stop and ask the lead rider (p. 61).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics): The lead rider will probably ask you to step a fewpaces downhill from the trail and stand quietly while theanimals pass (p. 61).
Step 2 (Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics): If you encounter other hikers or backpackersgoing uphill when you are going downhill, give them the right of-way (p. 61).
Step 3 (Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics): Step aside on a rock or a log to minimize your impact (p. 61).
Step 4 (Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics): If possible, campaway from trails and other visitors (p. 61).

pamphlet_excerpts: Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics: Extending courtesy to other outdoor visitors is a natural habit of backpackers (p. 61).
Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics Principle 2: If you carry amobile telephone for emergency communication, turn it off andstow it in your pack until you need (p. 61).
Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics Principle 3: Appreciate the company of those you meet on the trail and at campsites near yours, butrespect their desire for quiet and solitude (p. 61).

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics): The lead rider will probably ask you to step a fewpaces downhill from the trail and stand quietly while theanimals pass (p. 61).
Step 2 (Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics): If you encounter other hikers or backpackersgoing uphill when you are going downhill, give them the right of-way (p. 61).
Step 3 (Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics): Step aside on a rock or a log to minimize your impact (p. 61).
Step 4 (Leave No Trace & Outdoor Ethics): If possible, campaway from trails and other visitors (p. 61).
